questions.question: What is the typical duration of a Sprint in Scrum?
questions.explanation: A Sprint in Scrum typically lasts 2-4 weeks, providing a consistent timeframe for delivering increments of work.

questions.question: Which Agile methodology uses a visual board with columns to track work progress?
questions.explanation: Kanban uses a visual board with columns representing workflow stages to track and limit work in progress.

questions.question: In Scrum, who is responsible for maximizing the value of the product?
questions.explanation: The Product Owner is responsible for maximizing product value and managing the product backlog.

questions.question: What is a Daily Standup meeting in Agile?
options: A brief daily team synchronization meeting
A planning meeting for the next sprint
questions.explanation: The Daily Standup is a short daily meeting where team members synchronize activities and plan for the next 24 hours.

questions.question: Which Agile practice involves two programmers working together at one workstation?
questions.explanation: Pair programming has two developers work together at one computer, with one writing code and the other reviewing.

questions.question: What is the main focus of the Scrum Master role?
questions.explanation: The Scrum Master facilitates Scrum events, removes impediments, and helps the team follow Agile practices.

questions.question: In Kanban, what does WIP stand for?
questions.explanation: WIP stands for Work In Progress, which Kanban limits to improve flow and identify bottlenecks.

questions.question: What is a Product Backlog in Scrum?
options: A list of bugs found in testing
An ordered list of features and requirements
questions.explanation: The Product Backlog is a prioritized list of features, enhancements, and fixes needed for the product.

questions.question: Which Agile ceremony focuses on continuous improvement?
questions.explanation: The Sprint Retrospective allows the team to reflect on the process and identify improvements for the next sprint.

questions.question: What does a user story typically follow in format?
options: As a [role], I want [feature] so that [benefit]
questions.explanation: User stories follow the format: As a [role], I want [feature] so that [benefit], focusing on user value.

questions.question: Which Scrum ceremony is held at the start of a Sprint to select backlog items and plan the work?
questions.explanation: Sprint Planning opens each Sprint: the team selects Product Backlog items and builds a plan for delivering them.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the Sprint Review?
options: To demonstrate the completed increment to stakeholders and gather feedback
To assign blame for missed work
questions.explanation: The Sprint Review inspects the increment with stakeholders and adapts the Product Backlog based on feedback.

questions.question: In Extreme Programming, which practice requires writing a failing test before the production code?
questions.explanation: TDD is a core XP practice: write a failing test first, then write just enough code to make it pass, then refactor.

questions.question: Which Agile framework is specifically designed to coordinate many Agile teams across a large enterprise?
questions.explanation: The Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) provides structures like Agile Release Trains to scale Agile across large organizations.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an official Scrum role?
questions.explanation: Scrum defines only Product Owner, Scrum Master, and Developers; there is no Project Manager role because the team self-manages.

questions.question: What is a burndown chart used for in Agile projects?
questions.explanation: A burndown chart plots remaining work versus time, showing whether the team is on track to finish the Sprint scope.

questions.question: In Kanban, what does a cumulative flow diagram visualize?
options: The amount of work in each workflow stage over time
questions.explanation: A cumulative flow diagram shows how many items sit in each workflow stage over time, revealing bottlenecks and WIP growth.

questions.question: How many accountabilities (roles) does Scrum define?
questions.explanation: Scrum defines three accountabilities: Product Owner, Scrum Master, and Developers.

questions.question: What is a 'spike' in Agile development?
options: A sudden increase in team velocity
A time-boxed research activity to reduce technical uncertainty
questions.explanation: A spike is a time-boxed investigation or prototype used to answer a technical question or reduce uncertainty before estimating work.

questions.question: What does 'Definition of Ready' mean in Agile teams?
options: The product is ready to ship
The criteria a backlog item must meet before it can be pulled into a Sprint
questions.explanation: Definition of Ready is a shared checklist ensuring a backlog item is clear, estimated, and small enough before Sprint Planning.

questions.question: Which Agile method organizes all work around client-valued features built in short cycles?
questions.explanation: Feature-Driven Development (FDD) builds an overall model, then designs and builds small client-valued features in short iterations.

questions.question: What is a story point?
options: A fixed measure of one hour of work
A relative unit estimating effort, complexity, and risk of a user story
A count of lines of code
questions.explanation: Story points express relative effort and complexity compared to other stories, avoiding false precision of hour estimates.

questions.question: A client requires a fixed deadline, fixed budget, and fixed resources, but is willing to drop low-priority features if needed. Which Agile framework is designed for this?
questions.explanation: DSDM fixes time, cost, and quality while flexing features, using MoSCoW prioritization to drop lower-priority scope first.

questions.question: What is the maximum recommended length of a Daily Standup (Daily Scrum)?
questions.explanation: The Daily Scrum is time-boxed to 15 minutes to keep the team synchronized without disrupting the day's work.

questions.question: What is 'technical debt' in Agile software development?
options: The future rework cost created by choosing quick, suboptimal solutions
questions.explanation: Technical debt is the accumulated cost of shortcuts; like financial debt, it accrues 'interest' through slower future changes.

questions.question: The Agile Manifesto values 'individuals and interactions' over what?
questions.explanation: The first Agile Manifesto value statement is 'Individuals and interactions over processes and tools.'

questions.question: A team's sprint burndown stays flat for the first eight days, then drops sharply in the last two days when everything is marked done at once. What is the most likely underlying problem?
options: The team is consistently ahead of schedule
Stories are too large, so progress is only visible when whole items complete
The Sprint Goal should be cancelled
Velocity is artificially inflated by the chart
questions.explanation: A flat-then-cliff burndown usually means backlog items are too big to show daily progress; splitting stories smaller exposes real progress and risk earlier.

questions.question: After an Agile team grows from 6 to 12 members, velocity drops and stand-ups regularly exceed 30 minutes. Which principle best explains the productivity loss?
options: Parkinson's Law - work expands to fill the available time
Conway's Law - systems mirror the organization's communication structure
Communication paths grow quadratically with team size (n(n-1)/2)
Little's Law - throughput is limited by cycle time
questions.explanation: Communication channels grow as n(n-1)/2: 6 members = 15 paths, 12 = 66 paths. Coordination overhead, not effort, consumed the gain - so Agile favors small teams.

questions.question: Using Planning Poker on a modified Fibonacci scale, a team estimates a story at 8 points. A second, nearly identical story is judged to need roughly twice the effort. What should its estimate be?
questions.explanation: Story points are relative and follow Fibonacci values; the next value capturing 'roughly double 8' is 13 - 16 is not on the scale and 21 is nearly triple.

questions.question: An XP team integrates modules only at each iteration's end; conflicting changes repeatedly break the build for days. Which XP practice directly prevents this?
options: Continuous Integration - integrate and test the whole system many times a day
questions.explanation: Continuous Integration requires developers to merge and run the full build/test suite several times daily, so conflicts surface within hours, not weeks.

questions.question: A Kanban board shows the 'Testing' column permanently at its WIP limit while developers keep pulling new work that queues behind it. Applying the Theory of Constraints, what should the team do first?
options: Hire more developers to clear the queue
Raise the Testing WIP limit so more items can enter
Move Testing to the end of the sprint
Have developers swarm on the Testing bottleneck before pulling new work
questions.explanation: Throughput is set by the constraint (Testing). Adding upstream work or more WIP only lengthens the queue; the fix is to focus capacity on the bottleneck first.
